holidays.name: International Mud Day
holidays.description: A day for kids, and grown-ups who haven't forgotten how, to kick off their shoes and squish, splash, and slide through mud. Dirty hands and messy grins are the whole point.
holidays.origin: International Mud Day began in 2009. It grew out of a grassroots effort to encourage outdoor sensory play and connect children with nature. It started with groups in Australia and Nepal and has since spread to many countries.
holidays.funFact: Mud play is linked to healthier immune systems in kids. Being filthy really can be good for you.

holidays.name: National Waffle Iron Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble kitchen gadget that turns plain batter into crispy, syrup-catching squares. Dust off your waffle iron and put it to work. Waffles are a start, but hash browns, brownies, and grilled cheese also work.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance, and its creator is unknown. It is widely listed on June 29 as a tribute to the appliance itself rather than the waffles it makes.
holidays.funFact: The first U.S. patent for a waffle iron was granted to Cornelius Swarthout in 1869. His design was a stovetop model that flipped over the flame.

holidays.name: National Almond Buttercrunch Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy buttercrunch, the buttery toffee that gets a chocolate coating and a sprinkle of crunchy almonds. It's a sweet excuse to treat yourself or make a batch at home.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is celebrated every June 29 by candy lovers who like their toffee with plenty of crunch.
holidays.funFact: Toffee is made by cooking sugar and butter to the 'hard crack' stage, around 300°F. That's why it snaps when you bite it.
